citeAs: The EgoLife Team (2025). EgoLife: Towards Egocentric Life Assistant. arXiv:2503.03803.
creator: Jingkang Yang, Shuai Liu, Yuhao Dong, Binzhu Xie, Zitang Zhou, Ziyue Wang, Bei Ouyang, Zhengyu Lin, Zhongang Cai, Lei Yang, Joerg Widmer, Xiamengwei Zhang, Hongming Guo, Pengyun Wang, Sicheng Zhang, Marco Cominelli, Francesco Gringoli, Ziwei Liu, Bo Li, Yuanhan Zhang, Peiyuan Zhang, Fangzhou Hong (LMMs-Lab, NTU S-Lab)
description: EgoLife is a comprehensive 300-hour egocentric, interpersonal, multiview, and multimodal daily life dataset collected over one week with six participants living together. Each participant wore Meta Aria glasses recording approximately 8 hours of egocentric video daily, supplemented by 15 GoPro cameras and 2 mmWave devices for synchronized third-person perspective data. The dataset includes intensive annotations such as audio transcripts, visual-audio narrations, and the EgoLifeQA benchmark with 6,000 long-context, life-oriented question-answering tasks.
name: EgoLife Dataset
rai:annotationsPerItem: Caption annotations: 361K narration phrases (averaging 2.65 seconds per narration) merged into 25K merged captions, then into visual-audio captions. EgoLifeQA: 500 QA per participant (6 participants = 3,000 total QA; the benchmark reports 6,000 QA total including additional annotations). Each QA includes the question, answer, distractors, audio requirement flag, and look-back time (certification length).
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: QA candidates were filtered from ~100K per participant down to 1K high-quality questions (less than 1% of original pool), then further refined to 500 QA per participant. Only questions requiring information from at least 5 minutes prior were retained, with preference for longer dependencies and strong real-world relevance. Annotators also flagged whether audio was required and specified the look-back time (certification length) for each question.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: CapCut (ByteDance) video editing software with dubbing functions for caption annotation; SRT file format for QA annotation review synchronized with video playback.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three annotation types: (1) Transcript: audio from 6 participants merged, speech recognition applied, diarization algorithm used to differentiate speakers, then manually reviewed and refined per participant track. (2) Captions: videos split into 5-minute clips slowed to 0.8x speed; annotators provided continuous narrations covering all actions, interactions, and environmental details; narrations converted to text and reviewed. Initial 361K narrations merged into 25K captions using GPT-4o-mini, then expanded into visual-audio captions using GPT-4o with representative frames (1 FPS) and transcripts, verified by human annotators. (3) EgoLifeQA: prompts designed for 5 question types fed into GPT-4o to generate ~100K timestamped QA candidates per participant; provided to annotators as SRT files for filtering; only questions requiring information from at least 5 minutes prior retained; filtered to 1K high-quality questions per participant, then refined to 500 QA per participant with human-generated distractors.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is intentionally narrow in scope: primarily Chinese language (Beijing session), single scenario (Earth Day party preparation), and only six participants in a controlled environment. The paper acknowledges this sacrifices generalizability. The dataset is limited to specific cultural and linguistic contexts, though a Milan session with primarily English was added to partially address this. Activity categorization was automatically performed using GPT-4o, which may introduce model-specific biases.
rai:dataCollection: Six volunteers lived together for one week in a custom-designed environment called the EgoHouse. Each participant wore Meta Aria glasses capturing multimodal egocentric videos (~8 hours/day). 15 strategically placed GoPro cameras recorded third-person perspectives, and millimeter-wave radars provided spatial and motion data. Data was collected in Beijing, China (7-day session, primarily Chinese) and a one-day session in Milan, Italy (primarily English). Activities included discussions, shopping, cooking, socializing, and entertainment. Recordings were structured into three-hour segments due to storage limitations.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data includes: first-person egocentric video and audio from 6 Meta Aria glasses (MP4); third-person video from 15 GoPro cameras (MP4); IMU data (CSV); gaze data (CSV); millimeter-wave radar ADC data (CSV); WiFi CSI data (HDF5). Videos were recorded in three-hour segments. The Beijing dataset has 40+ hours of daily activities across 7 days; the Milan dataset adds ~6 hours from one day.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Seven-day data collection period (Beijing session); one additional day in Milan. The Beijing session is the primary dataset discussed in the paper.
rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Direct measurement, Passive Data Collection
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset intentionally starts with a narrow setting (single language/scenario) sacrificing some generalizability. The primary language is Chinese (Beijing session). The dataset covers only six participants in a controlled environment over one week. EgoGPT struggles with speech understanding (laughter, emotions) due to reliance on ASR-trained data. Identity recognition is limited—fine-tuning on Day-1 leads to overfitting to early observations. EgoRAG lacks multi-step reasoning and performs single-pass search without iterative refinement. The dataset is limited to indoor/controlled environments with recording permission required for outdoor locations.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Videos split into 5-minute clips and slowed to 0.8x speed for annotation. Videos split into 30-second clips for EgoGPT captioning. For EgoLifeQA evaluation, videos split into 30-minute segments for models that cannot process ultra-long videos. Activity categorization automatically performed using GPT-4o on visual-audio captions with timestamps. Caption annotations stored in SRT format for alignment with video.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Multi-view synchronization: video and signal data from multiple sources synchronized using timestamps via EgoSync codebase. De-identification (EgoBlur): all participant faces, bystander faces, and vehicle license plates were blurred; sensitive audio segments were muted; sensitive screen content was blurred. Audio processing: audio tracks merged and processed for clarity. mmWave signal preprocessing: CFAR (constant false alarm rate) detection algorithm applied to detect dynamic target signals. WiFi CSI data collected using AX-CSI platform from 802.11ax frames with 160 MHz bandwidth and 4x4 MIMO configuration.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The project is described as ongoing, with plans to expand to cover a broader range of languages, locations, and activities. The Beijing dataset is fully annotated; the Milan dataset will be detailed in an upcoming EgoLife blog series. The paper notes that a reliable annotation team partnership will continue for future EgoLife versions. The dataset card describes it as an "ongoing project."
rai:dataSocialImpact: EgoButler and EgoLifeQA could enhance human-AI interaction for personalized assistance and context-aware applications, supporting daily activities, personal organization, and contextual reminders—particularly beneficial for the elderly or those with cognitive challenges. In educational and professional settings, egocentric AI could facilitate learning, task tracking, and skill development. Privacy and ethical considerations are essential as the technology integrates into personal spaces; safeguards for data privacy and transparency in AI decision-making are key to positive societal reception.
rai:dataUseCases: Developing egocentric life AI assistants; long-context video understanding; multimodal egocentric video understanding; identity recognition and tracking; long-context question answering; habit analysis; interpersonal interaction pattern analysis; entity logging; event recall; task tracking; health habit monitoring; personalized recommendations; human behavior recognition; multimodal signal analysis; human-machine interaction research.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o: used to expand merged captions into visual-audio captions and to generate ~100K QA candidates per participant. GPT-4o-mini: used to merge 361K narration phrases into 25K coherent captions. Whisper (speech recognition): used to generate initial timestamped transcripts. Open-source diarization algorithm (Whisper Diarization): used to differentiate speakers. GPT-4o: used for activity categorization from visual-audio captions with timestamps.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains egocentric video of participants' daily lives including personal activities, conversations, and social interactions. Mitigation measures include: blurring of all participant faces, bystander faces, and vehicle license plates; muting of sensitive audio segments; blurring of sensitive screen content (passwords, personal data). All participants provided informed consent. Raw data is securely stored with anonymization applied throughout.

null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: The paper does not describe the demographics of the annotation team beyond noting that finding a reliable annotation team took two months and five trials.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not explicitly discuss missing data handling beyond noting that glasses are collected every 3 hours for upload (during which participants rest), but this is a collection protocol detail rather than missing data handling.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described in the paper for the dataset itself.
